newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends off peak, settles into new range.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends off peak, settles into new range.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended off its peak on Wednesday, trading a tight 0.7018-35 range after a session of reasonable two-way business, dealers said.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.7016/23 from 0.7032/39 early in the session. The Trade-Weighted Index was similarly soft, closing at 68.92 from 69.06 this morning.
"It's probably just settling into a new range," said one Auckland dealer.
"We've had some pretty good moves over the last two or three days and, with the Aussie settling down, both seem a little over-extended on their highs," he said.
But with the Reserve Bank's six monthly economic projections due next week, dealers did not expect the currency to waver too far outside its new range.
Base support is now expected to kick in at around US$0.6990-00 with resistance at 0.7050-60.
